html:
Between 1219 and 1221 the Mongols under Genghis Khan destroyed the Khwarazmian Empire, which ruled Central Asia and Iran. It was the Mongols' first great campaign in the Islamic world, and one of the most destructive in history.

It began with an outrage. In 1218 the governor of Otrar killed a Mongol trade caravan of some 450 men, and Shah Muhammad II then had one of Genghis's envoys killed. Genghis came west with a huge army of horsemen. The shah spread his troops among the cities, and the Mongols took them one by one:

  • Otrar, after a long siege
  • Bukhara in 1220, where Genghis is said to have told the people he was the punishment of God
  • Samarkand in 1220
  • Urgench, the capital, in 1221, after the Mongols flooded it from the Amu Darya
  • Merv and Nishapur in Khurasan in 1221, with the mass killing of their people

The shah fled and died on an island in the Caspian Sea. His son Jalal al-Din fought on until Genghis beat him on the Indus in 1221. The campaign opened the way to Iran, later the Ilkhanate, and to the raid of Jebe and Subutai through the Caucasus into the Russian steppe. The irrigation works of Khurasan took centuries to recover.
